newsitem.title: USA: Russia sticks to plan for 1996 Eurobond debut.
newsitem.headline: Russia sticks to plan for 1996 Eurobond debut.

text.p: Russia is sticking to its plans to issue a first tranche of Eurobonds later this year once it recieves a credit rating, First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin said on Wednesday.
"It is planned to do the first tranche before the end of the year," Potanin, who is in overall charge of the economy, told a news conference.
He said more details would be available once the rating process was completed.
Potanin said Russian officials have been meeting ratings agencies and Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Tuesday the rating could be announced within 10 days.
Russian MinFin bonds have been rising this week on rumours that the rating could be announced this week.
Russian officials have spoken of an initial issue of $300 million to $500 million and JP Morgan and SBC Warburg have been mandated to manage the issue.
